name: Kamikochi: Taisho Pond to Myojin Pond (上高地)
why: A flat walk up a clear river under the Hotaka peaks, from a pond of drowned trees to a shrine pond in the forest.
book: Kamikochi is open mid-April to mid-November. No private cars: park at Sawando or Hirayu and take the bus; buses from Matsumoto and Shin-Shimashima must be booked ahead. Get off at the Taisho-ike stop. Hotaka shrine charges a small fee to enter Myojin Pond.
water: Shops, cafes and toilets at Kappa Bridge and Myojin; the river water is not for drinking. Carry 1 litre.
dangers: Asian black bears live in the valley: ring a bell in the quiet stretches and keep food packed.
Do not feed the monkeys or leave food out.
Mornings are cold, near freezing in May and October: bring a warm layer.
turnaround: Check the last bus time at the terminal when you arrive; be back at Kappa Bridge one hour before it.

points.name: Taisho Pond
points.note: Made by an eruption of Mount Yake in 1915: dead trees still stand in the water. The path follows the left bank past Tashiro Pond, 1.2 km on.

points.name: Kappa Bridge
points.note: The wooden suspension bridge in the centre of Kamikochi, with the Hotaka range straight up the valley. Hotels, cafes and the visitor centre.

points.name: Myojin Bridge and Myojinkan
points.note: Out on the left bank past Konashidaira camp, 3 km. Cross Myojin Bridge to the shrine.

points.name: Myojin Pond
points.note: Two quiet ponds of spring water behind Hotaka shrine's inner sanctuary, under Mount Myojin. Back by the right-bank nature trail.

points.name: Kamikochi bus terminal
points.note: Past Dakesawa marsh and Kappa Bridge to the buses, 6 minutes beyond the bridge.
